newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SembCorp, SMRT, WorldCom in Singapore telecoms bid.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp, SMRT, WorldCom in Singapore telecoms bid.

text.p: Marine-based conglomerate SembCorp Ltd, state-owned railway Singapore MRT (SMRT) and WorldCom Inc of the United States said on Friday they would make a joint bid for a Singapore domestic telephone service licence.

SembCorp and SMRT announced in March they were contemplating bidding for a basic telecommunications licence, which would allow them to provide a fixed telephone service to rival the current local monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
The joint statement said on Friday, SembCorp and SMRT would together hold 65 percent of the bidding venture, with WorldCom holding the remaining 35 percent.
Two other consortiums have also said they will bid for a domestic licence.
On paper, the stronger is from a combination of British Telecom, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, state utility Singapore Power and state-owned Singapore Technologies Telemedia.
The other is from Britain's Cable & Wireless, HongKong Telecommunications Ltd, Singapore Press Holdings and Keppel Telecom.
The Singapore government has said it will award one or two licences next year for services to start from April 2000.
